utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al., thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today is Wednesday, the 4th of July, 2007. I would like to welcome all the parties that are present in this courtroom, the Prosecution, the representative of international organisations -- of the international organisation as well as the Defence teams of the accused, and all the people who are helping us in our work. I have four oral decisions to render. The first oral decision relates to the holding of the 65 ter hearing next Tuesday in the presence of the Prosecution, the Defence counsel, as well as the SLO of the Chamber, Mrs. Linda Murnane, and the legal officer who will attend, and will be present at a 65 ter hearing. The principal purpose of that hearing is to gather the parties about 98 bis, the procedure. Furthermore, during this hearing the following topics will be talked of: The time needed by the Defence if after the decision under 98 bis Rule, if the hypothesis would be that the trial continues with all the counts as maintained or other counts. So that meeting has as its main purpose to debate with parties on the time necessary for the Defence. Following the meeting that will be held next Tuesday, the legal officers will report to us what was said and the Chamber will render a decision regarding this. The second oral decision is on the admissibility of evidence through Witness BH. The Chamber rules today on admissibility of exhibits related to Witness BH who testified on the 24th, 25th, 26th of April, 2007, and 31st of May, 2007. I would like to make sure that the dates are well written down. 24, 25th, 26th of April, 2007 and 31 of May, 2007. The Chamber would like to admit Exhibit P 02616, submitted by the Prosecution as part of the list IC 00593, because they were presented to Witness BH and it shows sufficient indicia for relevancy, probative value and liability [as interpreted]. The Chamber has decided not to admit Exhibit 4D 00545 submitted by the Petkovic Defence as part of the list IC 00594, because it does not correspond to the provision of its decision of 13 July 2006 on the admission of evidence of exhibits. And I would like to add as well that the Chamber decided to admit Exhibit P 02577, submitted by the Accused Praljak. The Chamber notes that Exhibit P 09851, tendered by the Petkovic Defence, has already been admitted on 14 July 2007. 14 June 2007, correction. Third oral decision relating to the filing of the expert report by the Prosecution of Charles Siletic [as interpreted]. Mr. Sudetic, S-u-d-e-t-i-c. On the 23rd of May, 2007, the Prosecution submitted to the Trial Chamber as well as to the Defence an expert report of Mr. Charles Sudetic under Rule 94 bis of the Rules. The Prlic Defence counsel, Praljak, Petkovic, Coric, and Pusic, as a response on the 18th, 21st, 13, 22nd, 19th and 22nd of June, 2007 have opposed to the admission of this report, and they contested the expertise of the expert witness as well as the relevancy of the said report. The six Defence counsel requested to counter -- cross-examine Mr. Sudetic. The Chamber, having deliberated on this matter, believes that the report prepared by Mr. Charles Sudetic cannot be deemed to be an expert report because fundamentally it is a compilation of presidential transcripts and do not consist -- does not consist of an analysis which may help the Chamber to judge on a probative value and the relevancy of these transcripts. This is why the Chamber has decided to reject the request presented by the Prosecution. Last oral decision on the request of the Prlic request asking for an interlocutory appeal -- to an appeals certification, correction, of the 26th of June, 2007. Oral order, correction. The 3rd of July 2007, that is yesterday, the Defence of the accused Prlic has admitted -- filed a motion to ask the Chamber to certify an appeal of a decision that has been rendered on the 26th of June, 2007, on the application of guideline number 6 as stated in the decision on the admissibility of evidence on the 29th of November, 2006. The Chamber does not believe that it is necessary to wait for the response of the Prosecution to that effect. The Chamber decides that the motion of the Prlic Defence is inadmissible because it is irrelevant. In fact, on the 26th of June, 2007, the Chamber reminded the previous decisions on the application of guideline number 6. It was a reminder and not a decision per se. If the Prlic Defence wanted to contest the previous decisions on the interpretation of guideline number 6, it should have asked certification of appeal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of its anterior or previous decisions, and this within the time as seen in Article -- in Rule 73(C) of the Rules. Consequently, the motion is rejected. I believe that Mr. Kovacic wanted to intervene. Mr. Kovacic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to Your Honours and everybody else in the courtroom. Your Honour, I have been assigned on behalf of all the Defence teams to make a submission, an oral request, in fact, to the Trial Chamber. I'm not going to say demand or motion but a request to extend the deadline for a response to the three submissions made by the Prosecution, and they are submissions of the 27th of June, two, and one of the 29th of June, 2007. And I'd like to remind the Trial Chamber that it concerned the following motions: The first was the Prosecution motion to add exhibits to its exhibit list, and in fact that relates to the following documents, documents related to the accused -- well, I don't think I should say the name in open session, but anyway, it's a person who is not here any longer. I think you'll know who I mean, not to have to go into private session. And then Prosecution motion for admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis(B), and it is the request for the admission of documents related to the events in Vares municipality. And the third is the Prosecution motion for admission of documentary evidence, and here, Your Honours, it is 398 exhibits, and they are related to the structure of the HVO, the military sector of the HVO. I don't want to go into detail, too much details, but the last one is about 5.000 pages of documents, which would require hours and hours of diligent work. And the previous two are not as extensive. They're not such long documents, but they are very serious documents when it comes to analysis. As you know, we're going to have a break and go on holiday, all of us, and I think we -- well-deserved, and I don't want to keep anybody back here from going away on holiday because that will have a negative repercussion on our work in future. Somebody will quite simply end up in hospital. And I think that all the Defence teams are equally exhausted. Now, the other element is that we want to have a joint response to those motions, all -- on the part of all six Defence teams, and I'm sure you're quite clear as to the fact that this is impossible without putting into many hours of meetings or communication via telephone or e-mail or whatever because we have to dovetail our stands. But at any rate, even if the deadline is significantly extended, well, I think that if the deadline is extended I think that that will be a better thing for all of us. Not only for the Trial Chamber but for all the parties in these proceedings, and indeed for the Prosecution, because they'll be able to respond to one motion instead of six. So I think that that is reason enough. There are other reasons, but I don't want to take up any more court time, and I deem that these are sufficient reasons which merit an extension of the deadline. And we think that such a deadline will not hamper the Prosecution in any way. They will still have enough time to get through their own plans with regards to exhibits and documents, and I think that this will contribute to quality. Thank you, Your Honours. I do apologise. I was going too fast my colleagues tell me, but I forgot to say that we would like to extend the deadline until Monday, the 10th of September, 2007, which will give us three weeks. You have already extended the deadline until the 12th or 14th of July for the other submission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, good afternoon to all of you, first of all, and to everyone in the courtroom. Your Honour, it has not been -- the Prosecution acknowledges -- to acknowledge the obvious that we have been trying to make a number of filings. We set our own deadlines and our own schedule to try to deal with a number of matters before the summer recess. It has not been our intention, is not our intention to, by those filings, create undue pressure on the Defence during the holiday season if we can call it that, the summer recess. So I want that to be clear, number one, that that's -- certainly hasn't been tactical but the Prosecution, as a matter of its own internal case management has sought to try to get as many of these matters filed off of our table so to speak before the summer recess as possible but at the same time it has not about our intention by doing so to create an unnecessary or unreasonable burden on the Defence. We do not object to an extension of time. As to the specific date of the 10th of September, Your Honour, my only concern is this and it's more general than just this one: Everyone in the courtroom knows that we will be seeking, of course, to finish the Prosecution case this fall. It will be virtually impossible for us to conclude our case without knowing what -- what of our case -- what of your evidence has been admitted. So there is building to state -- again to state the obvious perhaps, there is building a substantial backlog of material and motions. For example, I know that the Jablanica 92 bis motion was filed in February, has not yet been ruled upon now in July. So I just flag the issue -- not the issue. I flag the concern for the Chamber. The Prosecution will not be in a position to make any informed decision on finalising its case or resting its case until its evidence has been admitted or not. So we do not oppose an extension of time. We do want the Defence to have a summer holiday just as we are looking forward to one ourselves, but I can only tell the Chamber that the longer these deadlines and decisions go out, the more difficult it will be to complete the case in the fall. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber, as you may have noticed, has decided -- or deliberated, and received the request -- a motion of the Defence which is to request an extension of delays because the Defence received three motions that are very important to them. One request is of the 27th of June, one regarding added exhibit on the list, and a second motion is a motion regarding the admissibility of evidence under Rule 92 bis, and a third motion of the Prosecution of the 29th of June on a request of admissibility of 398 documents on the military structure of the HVO, that motion counting approximately 5.000 pages. The Chamber believes on the one hand that in a couple of days the Tribunal will begin its summer recess, and the analysis of these documents would require of the Defence an important workload, and also joint responses have to be which would call upon the Defence to organise internal meetings between them and the accused. The Chamber believes that the motion presented by Mr. Kovacic on behalf of all the Defence counsel is admissible, and since there are no major obstacles presented by the Prosecution, since they've also mentioned that it is in their interest know what is presented, this is why the Prosecution talked about the Jablanica motion. For all these motives, the Chamber decided to extend the deadline to the 10th of September, 2007. I would also like to mention, to invite -- I would like to invite the Prosecution to give us their final schedule for the witnesses that are about to come. According to us, the Defence has between 68 -- the Prosecution has between 68 and 69 hours to present their case, and the Chamber would like to know who are going to be the witnesses who are going to be called in October in order to be able on the one hand to know who is going to be coming, who is not coming. We have already requested it. It was not done, and I would like to remind on my behalf, because the Chamber has not deliberated on this, but I would like to say that the strategy of the Prosecution, who has the burden of the proof is on the Prosecution, and that under the rule the Prosecution has to prepare the files, and while they prepare their files, of course, they have to inform the Chamber of the planning and of the witnesses that are to come. It is very important for the Judges of the Chamber to know who are going to be the witnesses that will be coming, because it may happen that amongst the witnesses, some of them may not come, and others could be here and called to testify, but we do not have the list. We do not know who these people are. So once again, Mr. Scott, we are counting on you, and we would like to reiterate our request. Up until now we have not made a decision, but we will have to render a decision shortly on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you. The Prosecution is certainly mindful of the request the Chamber has made in the past and have been working on that matter and in fact I was working on it very actively this morning. I anticipate that we would make such a filing on Monday, if that's agreeable to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. That would be an excellent news, because before taking a few days off we could take a look at your document and spend the entire vacation reading this document. If the document arrives on Monday that would be an excellent news.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know if anyone wants to spend their holidays reading it, Your Honour, but that was partly our thought that if we could something in the Chamber's hands and in the Defence's hands before the recess, then everyone would be able to consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: President, if I may be heard for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. President, good afternoon, Your Honours. With respect to your oral decision on my motion for my request for certification, I assume there will be something in writing. I assume. I heard two things. One, that it was irrelevant, which would mean it goes to the merit, and then also it was tardy. With respect to the tardiness, as I indicated on the record that I was obviously -- I misunderstood the ruling, and therefore based on that, obviously it would have been tardy and it would have been a lack of due diligence on my part. Therefore, if that is the fundamental reason for denying the request for certification, I would suggest and I would urge the Trial Chamber to sanction me as being counsel in charge of this defence for failing to protect my client's rights, as opposed to punishing my client over failing to -- because his lawyer, his chosen lawyer, failed to file for certification on an important issue. So if those are the reasons, I would ask the Trial Chamber to reconsider. Sanction me, but don't sanction Mr. Prlic. If on the other hand, it's on the merits, then I understand it's on the merits and that's fine. I just want to make sure the record is clear, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We'll reconsider your application or the application you've just made, but as far as I'm concerned, the meaning of the oral ruling we've just rendered is the following: The guidelines included in the decision could have been challenged at the time of the decision, and it was not the case. That's what we wanted to say. I'm going to ask the registrar to pull down the blinds -- or, rather, the usher to pull down the blinds and to have the witness brought in because we've been spending a lot of time on all these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.08 p.m.,
